title: Parallel seats proven, and the concurrency limit is disclosed on /sessions/read and Seats
description:
SPIDR child 3 of parent task-4423d2a4c3084d579c132b253d36b502 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-04). dependsOn child 2 task-1d7b9df2579c491992b55de791c99f4f: the "a HARD-dependent node is not staffed" half of this row's proof needs that gate to exist.

This is the parent's DoD 3. OWNER DECISION 2026-09-04 (asked and answered in the planning REPL): EXPOSE THE EXISTING ENV KNOB. Do not build a durable store-backed per-project setting and do not add an operator command for it - the smallest production-reachable slice (global rail 16, delivery bias). If a durable setting is wanted later it is a separate row.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb - the parent's description overstates this gap:
- PARALLEL STAFFING ALREADY WORKS. `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts:339-371` collects every READY unclaimed step in one pass and spawns each in turn, breaking only at `if (staffing.activeCount() >= config.maxAgents) break` (line 356). There is no one-at-a-time serialization to remove.
- THE LIMIT ALREADY DEFAULTS TO 2. `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/wrapper-knobs.ts:30` `const DEFAULT_MAX_AGENTS = 2`; line 72 reads env `MOE_WRAPPER_MAX_AGENTS` with that default and a floor of 1. It reaches the wrapper via `agent-wrapper-main.ts:259` `maxAgents: knobs.maxAgents`.
- WHAT IS MISSING IS DISCLOSURE AND PROOF. `apps/daemon/src/http/sessions-read.ts` (SESSIONS_READ_PATH "/sessions/read", SessionsView at line 37) publishes sessions only - `grep -n maxAgents apps/daemon/src/http/sessions-read.ts` = 0 hits. The browser cannot tell an operator why only two nodes are moving.
- THE BROWSER PATH IS ALREADY OPEN: `apps/control-room/src/live/live-sessions.ts` posts `/sessions/read` with EXACTLY `{}` and shapes the answer verbatim (it will REJECT an unexpected member - read its decoder before adding one); `/sessions/read` is already in `apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts:37`; Seats renders in `apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/activity-screens.tsx` off `live-ops.tsx`.
- NO NEW COMMAND KIND, so no 8-touchpoint roster backfill: this row extends an existing READ's response shape only.
definitionOfDone: `POST /sessions/read` discloses the effective concurrency limit and the current active-seat count as typed members of SessionsView; a daemon test asserts the limit equals the wrapper's configured maxAgents (default 2) and that it changes when MOE_WRAPPER_MAX_AGENTS is set, so the disclosed number is the REAL knob and not a hard-coded 2.

Wrapper test over the real staffing loop: a surface offering TWO independent READY unclaimed node.deliver steps produces TWO spawn reports in a SINGLE pass, asserted before either child exits (assert the spawned array length and both work-item ids, not just that spawning happened).

Wrapper test for the dependency gate's effect: a surface where node b is BLOCKED on `depends:a` yields exactly ONE spawn (a), and on the next pass after a is ACCEPTED, b IS spawned. Assert the work-item id in each pass, and assert the count line - a pass that silently spawns zero must fail this test.

The limit is honoured under pressure: with maxAgents = 2 and THREE independent READY steps, exactly two spawn in the pass and the third is not spawned. Assert the third's absence by work-item id, not by array length alone.

apps/control-room reads and renders the limit on Seats (live-sessions.ts decoder accepts the new member without rejecting the response; activity-screens.tsx shows it in operator words). A control-room test asserts the rendered sentence for a limit of 2 with 2 active, and for a limit of 2 with 0 active.

Mutation drill recorded in a step note: change the wrapper's break to `>` instead of `>=`, confirm the three-READY limit test goes RED, restore, prove the restore with `git diff` on the tracked file (quote the empty diff).
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: DO NOT build a durable per-project seat limit, a new command kind, or an operator setting UI. Owner decision 2026-09-04: expose the existing MOE_WRAPPER_MAX_AGENTS knob. A new command kind would drag in the full roster backfill this row is explicitly scoped to avoid.

`live-sessions.ts` shapes the /sessions/read answer VERBATIM and will refuse an unexpected member. Change the decoder and the daemon response in the same row, and assert the round trip - a daemon-only change silently breaks the Seats screen (memory ui-connect-everything-built-2026-09-02: new daemon read = 8 touchpoints + a .js bridge; this is a shape extension, so at minimum the port, its .js bridge if new, the decoder and the renderer).
FEATURES ONLY (inherited from the parent): no security-boundary or policy work.
Never restart the wrapper to unstick a seat while testing live (claim TTL is 30 min; memory real-seat-cannot-release-its-claim-2026-09-04).

implementationPlan.description: PROVE PARALLEL STAFFING, in apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.test.ts. These arms are this row's real deliverable — the behaviour exists but nothing pins it, so a later refactor could serialise staffing silently. (a) TWO INDEPENDENT READY NODES: a surface offering two READY unclaimed `node.deliver` steps with no dependencies produces TWO spawn reports in a SINGLE pass, asserted before either child exits (assert the spawned array length AND both work-item ids, not merely that spawning happened — an arm asserting only `length > 0` passes on a serial loop). (b) THE LIMIT IS HONOURED: with `maxAgents: 2` and THREE independent READY steps, exactly two spawn and the third does not — assert the third's ABSENCE by its work-item id, not by array length alone, so a pass cannot come from spawning a different pair. (c) `maxAgents: 1` staffs exactly one and leaves the rest, proving the break is the limit and not an accident of ordering.
implementationPlan.note:
Added `describe("the wrapper staffs seats in parallel")` to apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.test.ts (2013 -> 2155 lines). NO production file touched — the staffing loop is unchanged, per step 1(c).

WHY A NEW HARNESS AND NOT THE EXISTING ARM. agent-wrapper.test.ts:186 already staffs 2, but off the LIVE bootstrap surface and asserting only `expect(report.spawned).toHaveLength(2)` — no work-item ids, so it passes for the wrong pair, and it cannot vary maxAgents because the module-level `wrapper` is fixed at 2 and its claims persist across the file. Hence three isolated projects (proj-wrapper-parallel-{two,limit,one}), each with its own store.

THE HARNESS (2 helpers + 2 one-liners, modelled on the existing nodePort at :736):
- `nodeStepsPort(live, reader, projectId, nodes)` — layers synthesized `node.deliver` steps over the LIVE surface (`...surface`) so every other frame member keeps its production shape, and reads `claim`/`claimAggregateVersion` back out of the REAL claim ledger (`readWorkClaimLedger`) rather than remembering them in the test. That is what makes a SECOND pass see what the first pass durably claimed — needed by step 3.
- `nodeWrapper(harness, port, maxAgents, prefix)` — real `deps: harness.isolated.provide()`, so session.open + work.claim are real dispatches through the committed adapter. `spawnAgent` returns `exit: new Promise(() => undefined)`, i.e. the child NEVER exits, so every assertion below reads a pass whose children are still alive (the DoD's "asserted before either child exits").
- `deliver(nodeRef)` calls the PRODUCTION `workItemIdFor("node.deliver", ...)`, not a hand-written `node.deliver@x` literal, so the ids in the expectations cannot drift from the producer.

THE THREE ARMS, and what each would let through if written the lazy way:
(a) "spawns TWO independent READY nodes in ONE pass, naming both work items" — two READY unclaimed nodes, maxAgents 2.
    `expect(report.spawned.map(e => e.workItemId)).toEqual([deliver("par-a"), deliver("par-b")])` (ids, ordered), outcomes `["SPAWNED","SPAWNED"]`, `report.active).toBe(2)` — two seats live AT THE SAME MOMENT, which a serial loop cannot produce. Plus the durable second opinion: both claims exist and `new Set(holders).size).toBe(2)`, so it is two distinct agent sessions, not one seat counted twice.
(b) "honours maxAgents 2 against THREE READY nodes: the third is not spawned" — THIS is the arm step 8's `>=`->`>` drill targets.
    `.toEqual([deliver("lim-a"), deliver("lim-b")])` pins the exact pair in order (a bare length 2 also passes for {b,c} or a duplicate), `.not.toContain(deliver("lim-c"))` is the explicit absence-by-id the DoD asks for, and `claims.get(deliver("lim-c"))).toBeUndefined()` proves the break happened BEFORE the claim rather than after a claim the report merely omits.
(c) "honours maxAgents 1 ... exactly one, and it is the first" — the SAME three-step shape yielding exactly one proves the break is the LIMIT and not an accident of ordering; both left-behind items are named and asserted unclaimed.

Deliberately NOT relying on the loop's existing filters: every step in these surfaces is `node.deliver` with `missing: []`, so HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS, the `session.*` skip and the node.deliver-first sort cannot be what produces any expected count.

implementationPlan.description: PROVE THE DEPENDENCY GATE'S EFFECT ON STAFFING, same file — this is the half of DoD 3 that closes the loop between task-1d7b9df2's surface change and the wrapper. (a) A surface where node b is BLOCKED with `missing: ["depends:a"]` and node a is READY yields exactly ONE spawn, and it is a — assert by work-item id. (b) On the NEXT pass, with a's review accepted so the surface now reports b READY, b IS spawned. Assert the work-item id in each pass. (c) Assert the spawn COUNT in each pass explicitly: a pass that silently spawns zero must FAIL these arms rather than pass them vacuously (global rail 1). Note the loop already skips HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS and `session.*` kinds and orders `node.deliver` first (agent-wrapper.ts:348-357) — build the fake surface so those existing filters are not what produces the expected counts, or the arm proves the sort order rather than the gate.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT UNDER TEST HERE — stated plainly so nobody grades this arm for the wrong thing. task-1d7b9df2 owns and proved the SURFACE half (affordance-read.ts:442-452 folds the review ledger, emits `depends:<nodeKey>` and flips the node to BLOCKED; 7 arms in affordance-read.test.ts, plus the bidirectional roster arm in work-labels.test.ts). This row owns the WRAPPER half: what the staffing loop does with that report. The stub surface is therefore the wrapper's INPUT, exactly as the plan directs; it is not a second implementation of the gate.

ARM 1 "leaves a dependency-blocked node alone with a seat FREE, then staffs it once READY", maxAgents 2, two passes on ONE wrapper:
- PASS 1: `spawned` length 1 and `.toEqual([deliver("dep-a")])` — the id, not just a count. `claims.get(deliver("dep-b"))` is `undefined`, so dep-b was never claimed.
- THE LOAD-BEARING ASSERTION is `expect(first.active).toBe(1)` with maxAgents 2. A free seat was available and dep-b still was not staffed, so what withheld it is the DEPENDENCY and not the limit. Without this, the arm could not distinguish "the gate worked" from "the arm is really a second copy of the maxAgents test", and a pass that silently spawned zero would also have to fail (`toHaveLength(1)`), which is global rail 1's explicit ask in step 3(c).
- PASS 2 (`accepted.add("dep-a")`, so the surface now reports dep-b READY): `spawned` length 1, `.toEqual([deliver("dep-b")])`, `second.active` 2. Plus `.not.toContain(deliver("dep-a"))` and `claims.get(deliver("dep-a"))` still `{status:"OPEN", version:1}` — proof the second pass is the DEPENDENCY MOVING, not the first pass replaying: dep-a's claim and seat from pass 1 are still live, so it is correctly skipped.

THE EXISTING FILTERS ARE NOT WHAT PRODUCES THE COUNTS (the step's explicit warning). Every step in the surface is `node.deliver` with no HUMAN_ONLY or `session.*` kind, so those skips cannot fire; and the BLOCKED node is listed FIRST in the array, so the node.deliver-first sort cannot be what "explains" dep-a spawning. The loop reaches dep-b, reads `status !== "READY"`, and continues.

ARM 2 "spells the blocking token exactly as the production surface emits it": reads apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts as SOURCE TEXT and asserts it contains `.map((nodeRef) => \`depends:${nodeRef}\`)`. The wrapper branches on `status`, never on `missing`, so this token is realism rather than mechanism — which is precisely why it needs a guard: without it the stub could drift to a token production no longer emits and these arms would keep passing while rehearsing a dead shape. A rename now reds HERE with a pointer, instead of silently.

implementationPlan.description: DISCLOSE THE LIMIT ON THE DAEMON READ. apps/daemon/src/http/sessions-read.ts: `SessionsView` (:37-43) gains the effective concurrency limit and the current active-seat count. SOURCE THE LIMIT HONESTLY — measured at plan time: the wrapper and the daemon are SEPARATE PROCESSES (agent-wrapper-main.ts and daemon-main.ts are distinct entry points), but apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-main.ts builds ONE `childEnv` (:276) and spawns BOTH children with it (:201 daemon, :326 wrapper), so the daemon's `process.env` carries the same MOE_WRAPPER_MAX_AGENTS the wrapper parsed. Therefore: take the value by calling the EXISTING `readWrapperKnobs` (orchestrator/wrapper-knobs.ts:61) rather than re-parsing the variable — a second parser would drift from its strict NaN refusal (wrapper-knobs.ts:1-8 explains why a lenient parse is catastrophic here). Pass it in through `SessionsReadOptions` and supply it at the composition site daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts:353, so the port stays injectable and testable rather than reading process.env itself. NAME IT AS WHAT IT IS in the field name and its doc comment: the CONFIGURED limit this daemon was launched with, not a live observation of the wrapper — a daemon started standalone would report a limit no wrapper is honouring, and the comment must say so rather than let a reader assume it is measured.
implementationPlan.note:
SHAPE, in apps/daemon/src/http/sessions-read.ts (135 -> 172 lines):
- NEW exported `SessionsConcurrency { activeSeats, configuredAgentLimit }`, and `SessionsView` gains ONE top-level member `concurrency: SessionsConcurrency`. Nested rather than two flat members so the browser's exact-arity top level grows by exactly one key and the nested guard mirrors the `totals` guard already there.
- `SessionsReadOptions.configuredAgentLimit: number` is REQUIRED and deliberately NOT defaulted. A member falling back to the wrapper's own default would publish "2" from a daemon that was never told the limit, and no arm could tell that apart from the real knob — the compiler is what enumerates the construction sites instead. It did: `pnpm typecheck` named exactly two, both in sessions-read.test.ts (step 5's own file); ZERO production sites broke.
- `activeSeats` is counted in the existing session loop from ledgers this read ALREADY folds: `liveness === "LIVE" && holding.length > 0`. `holding` was hoisted out of the object literal into a const to be counted; its expression is byte-identical. A paired browser holds nothing and an expired seat is not working, so neither is a seat the wrapper could have staffed instead. `read()` stays under 50 lines.

NAMED AS WHAT IT IS, per the step's non-negotiable. The `SessionsConcurrency` doc comment states in full: `configuredAgentLimit` is CONFIGURED, never observed — the MOE_WRAPPER_MAX_AGENTS this DAEMON PROCESS was launched with; `moe up` spawns daemon and wrapper from one child environment so they agree in the launched configuration, but a standalone daemon (or one beside a separately-launched wrapper) reports a limit NO WRAPPER IS HONOURING; nothing here measures the wrapper. `activeSeats` is marked as the measured half, and the comment states it can lag the wrapper's in-process count by one pass because a seat counts from claim commit, not child start.

SOURCING, at daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts:369 (the site was at :353 at plan time; the file has grown since):
  configuredAgentLimit: readWrapperKnobs(process.env).maxAgents,
with `import { readWrapperKnobs } from "./orchestrator/wrapper-knobs.js";` (the .js bridge ALREADY EXISTS — `ls` confirms wrapper-knobs.js; no new bridge). No second parser: the value comes from the wrapper's own strict reader, so it inherits the NaN refusal wrapper-knobs.ts:1-8 exists to make. process.env is read at the COMPOSITION site, not inside the port, which is exactly what keeps the port injectable and lets step 5 prove the disclosed number is the knob and not a literal 2.

DISCLOSED CONSEQUENCE, deliberate, not an oversight. `readWrapperKnobs` THROWS `WRAPPER_ENV_INVALID: <name>` on a malformed value, and it parses four variables, not one. So a daemon launched with a typo'd MOE_WRAPPER_MAX_AGENTS / _INTERVAL_MS / _MAX_ITEM_ATTEMPTS / MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS now refuses to compose instead of serving a wrong or defaulted limit. That is fail-closed and names the variable, matches what the wrapper already does with the same env under `moe up`, and is the alternative to the lenient second parse the plan explicitly rejects. Measured: `grep -rn 'MOE_WRAPPER_' apps packages --include=*.ts` shows no test or production path setting these to a non-integer outside wrapper-knobs.test.ts's own `readWrapperKnobs({...})` literals, so nothing existing is disturbed.

New `describe("the sessions read discloses the concurrency limit")` with 6 arms; the two pre-existing construction sites (:42, :56) gained `configuredAgentLimit: 2` — those are the exact sites step 4's typecheck named, so the compiler's enumeration is now closed.

(a) "publishes the limit the WRAPPER's parser read, and it MOVES with the variable". The value is not a number typed into the test: it is `readWrapperKnobs({ MOE_WRAPPER_MAX_AGENTS: "5" }).maxAgents` and `...: "7"`, the SAME production parser the composition site calls. Asserts 5 then 7 through the same port. (b) "falls back to the wrapper's documented default of 2 when the variable is unset" — `readWrapperKnobs({}).maxAgents` is asserted to be 2 FIRST (so the arm fails loudly if the default ever moves) and then that the port publishes it.
(c) "counts an active seat as a LIVE seat that HOLDS work, and nothing else" — five seats, four claims, `concurrency` `toEqual({ activeSeats: 2, configuredAgentLimit: 2 })`. THREE near-misses each excluded for a DIFFERENT reason, so the count cannot pass by accident: a live seat whose only claim EXPIRED, a live-but-expired-bearer seat holding a live claim, and a CLOSED seat. (d) "reports zero active seats on an empty ledger, and still discloses the limit" — `{ activeSeats: 0, configuredAgentLimit: 4 }`; 4, not 2, so the empty case still proves the knob.
(e) "keeps every refusal frame at its EXACT three keys, with no concurrency member" — the real port's catch path (`readSessions` throws) plus SESSIONS_READ_CAPABILITY_DENIED and SESSIONS_READ_PROJECT_MISMATCH through `handleSessionsReadRequest`. A refusal that grew a concurrency member would stop matching live-sessions.ts:66's exact-arity `["code","layer","outcome"]` refusal decode and surface in the browser as a bad response instead of a refusal.
(f) "takes the limit from readWrapperKnobs at the composition site, not from a literal" — arms (a)-(d) only prove the PORT publishes what it is GIVEN. This one reads daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts as source text and asserts it contains `configuredAgentLimit: readWrapperKnobs(process.env).maxAgents`. Without it, a `configuredAgentLimit: 2` typed into the composition satisfies every other arm here and discloses a lie on any daemon launched with a different value — the wiring, not the port, would be the hard-code.
